text:
Will Smith is 21, plays 19 minutes a night for the Sharks, and has 19 points in 28 games. That is ahead of where most forwards picked near him land: the median for forwards taken second to sixth overall is 0.47 points a game in their first full season, and he is at 0.68 in his third. The talent is not in question. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 98th percentile among forwards for chances from the home-plate area last season.

What is in question right now is the puck luck around him. San Jose has scored 7.6 fewer goals than its chances deserve with Smith on the ice, one of the biggest gaps in the league, and his points per 60 minutes sit below the bottom of our talent range. The other part is less flattering: he is pointless in four straight, his minutes have dropped to about 14 and 15 in the last three games, and Evolving-Hockey flagged last season that opponents get more with him out there.

Watch the ice time. If it climbs back toward 20, the bounces should start finding him.
